name: Librum
description: TLS cert validation disabled app-wide (QSslSocket::QueryPeer) including the update download; .zip installed via an Administrator-elevated batch script with zero integrity check. [Opus-verified: CONFIRMED-D]

later_review_audit.description: The updater’s request builder uses QueryPeer, the downloaded archive is handed to an elevated unpack-and-install batch path, and the app restarts. No independent payload signature/hash is shown in the retained update flow.
limitations: Source review is limited to the retained commit and does not establish released-artifact or current-upstream behavior.

original_evidence.text: | Librum | https://github.com/Librum-Reader/Librum.git | 5fdac34 / 2024-07-01 | Y | check:Y (auto on launch) / install:N (user clicks "Update") | Y | https, **TLS validation effectively disabled** (`QSslSocket::QueryPeer` instead of default `VerifyPeer` on a client socket — handshake proceeds even if the cert fails validation) | N | **none** — response bytes written straight to a `.zip`, no hash/signature check anywhere | N/A — no verification performed | `src/infrastructure/persistance/app_info_access.cpp:70-77` `createRequest()`: `sslConfiguration.setPeerVerifyMode(QSslSocket::QueryPeer)` (same weakened config reused across `dictionary_access.cpp`, `authentication_access.cpp`, `library_storage_access.cpp`, etc.); `:38-44` `downloadBinaries()` GETs `{domain}/binary/{packageName}.zip`; `src/application/services/app_info_service.cpp:118-131` `processDownloadedBinaryData`→`saveBinaryDataToFile`; `:66-84` `unpackAndInstallBinaries()` shells out to `unzip_and_move.bat`, which **"queries Administrator rights"** and overwrites the installed binaries — no integrity check anywhere; trigger: `src/presentation/settings/updatesPage/MUpdatesAvailable.qml:103` `AppInfoController.updateApplication()` |
